hook: Asha buys 50 samosas for {buy} and sells them all for {sell}. Did she do well?
define: **Profit** is what you have left after paying your costs. If you end up with less, that is a **loss**. **Return** is the profit as a percentage of what you put in. It lets you compare small and big amounts.
paper: A gain or loss on something you still hold is a **paper** gain or loss. It becomes **realised** only when you sell.
analogy: Think of a tea stall. You spend {buy} on milk, tea and sugar. Customers pay {sell}. The extra money is your profit. Return tells you how hard each rupee worked.
worked: Asha's profit is {profit1}. Her return is {ret1}: that is {profit1} earned on {buy} put in. On a bad day she sells for {lowSell}. That is a loss of {lossAbs}, and a return of {ret2}.
predict.q: Your {startAmt} falls by {fall}. What rise brings it back to {startAmt}?
predict.explain: It needs a rise of {needGain}, not {fall}. After the fall you hold {afterFall}. To get back to {startAmt}, that {afterFall} must double.
tradeoff: A big percentage on a small amount can be fewer rupees than a small percentage on a big amount. A gain of {smallPct} on {smallBase} is {smallGain}. A gain of {bigPct} on {bigBase} is {bigGain}. Always look at both the rupees and the percentage.
mistake: Many people think a fall of {fall} and a rise of {fall} cancel out. They do not. {startAmt} falls to {afterFall}, then rises to only {afterRise}.
formula: Return = (value now - value you paid) ÷ value you paid. To recover from a fall of x, you need a rise of x ÷ (1 - x).
check.profit_loss_01.stem: Ravi buys a cap for {buy} and sells it for {sell}. What is his profit?
check.profit_loss_01.why: Profit is what you sell for minus what you paid. {sell} minus {buy} is {answer}.
check.profit_loss_02.stem: Sana buys shares worth {buy}. Later they are worth {now}. What is her return?
check.profit_loss_02.why: Return is profit divided by what you paid. Here {profit} divided by {buy} is {answer}. Dividing by the new value is a common slip.
check.profit_loss_03.stem: Asha gains {g1} on {b1}. Imran gains {g2} on {b2}. Who had the higher return?
check.profit_loss_03.opt.b: Imran, because he gained more rupees
check.profit_loss_03.why: Return compares the gain to the amount put in. Asha earned {r1} and Imran earned {r2}. Imran made more rupees, but on a much bigger amount.
check.profit_loss_04.stem: A price falls by {fall}. What rise brings it back to where it started?
check.profit_loss_04.why: After a fall of {fall} you hold half of what you started with. To double it again you need a rise of {answer}.
check.profit_loss_05.stem: A price falls by {fall}. What rise is needed to get back to the start?
check.profit_loss_05.why: A fall of {fall} leaves you with 80 out of every 100. To get back to 100, you need 20 more on top of 80. That is a rise of {answer}.
glossary.profit.def: Money left after paying all your costs.
glossary.loss.def: When you end up with less money than you started with.
glossary.return.def: Profit as a percentage of the money you put in.
glossary.paper_gain.def: A gain or loss on something you still hold and have not sold.
glossary.realised.def: A gain or loss that is locked in because you sold.
